launcher_icon._doc: The launcher icon, generated from this declaration by 1_cicd/src/scripts/cloud-android-launcher-icons.py (pattern + category colours + glyphs in 1_cicd/src/data/launcher-icons.json). Never edit the generated res files.

image_viewer._doc: #1741 Cloud Browser is an image viewer: the manifest's VIEW and SEND filters on image/* (content:// and file://) are held equal to this declaration by ImageViewerManifestTest, and every extension here must be a type the fleet's FileTypeRouter (ab_cloud-libs-shared editor-types.json, viewer media, format image) already routes, so Cloud Drive's file-type routing and Android's Open with see the same set. The page is imagepage (ImagePage.kt) in the browser's own libs:web-core web view. convert_pdf_action is the fleet door for 'convert this file to PDF': a fleet app (Cloud Drive's Convert section) fires it with the file as data (image or HTML) and the browser opens it and raises the print framework (Save as PDF); it is signature-guarded like the agent door. Printing is the platform print path (PrintManager + WebView.createPrintDocumentAdapter), not an in-process renderer: one-pdf-engine-guard.json::print_path records it.

name: cloud-browser
description: Diego's Cloud Browser — standalone WebView-based browser Android app. Lifted from Cloud SuperApp's libs:browser into its own focused APK. Multi-tab session persistence (BrowserTabPrefs), in-app URL bar, dark-chrome WebView host. Build via Nix devShell, one APK out.

signing._doc: ONE shared Cloud-constellation signing key for ALL Android apps (Cloud-Comms hub+forks, Cloud-Nav, Cloud-Wallet, Cloud-Browser, Cloud-IDE, Cloud-SuperApp). The SAME key signs every app so cross-app signature-IPC + the in-app fleet updater never hit a signature mismatch. KEY LOCATION (raw credential + sops passwords live ONLY in the vault repo): Shared/Providers/D_TOOLS-DEVICES/d2-android/release.jks (OU=Cloud Constellation) + Shared/Providers/D_TOOLS-DEVICES/d2-android/signing.secrets.yaml. build.sh::_resolve_signing resolves $VAULT_DIR (default ~/git/cloud-vault) + sops-decrypts the passwords, exporting ANDROID_KEYSTORE_FILE/ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD/ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS/ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD which the gradle signingConfig reads. CI does the same via a vault checkout + the SOPS_AGE_KEY secret. THERE IS NO FALLBACK: if the key is unavailable the build FAILS LOUD.

diagnostics._doc: On-device DevControlServer diagnostics → cloud sink. Baked into BuildConfig.LOG_SINK_URL / LOG_SINK_STREAM by app/build.gradle. Empty url = cloud push disabled.

toolchain._doc: Pinned for reproducibility — all derived in flake.nix. Bump here, rebuild devShell.

libs:web-core._doc: #1371 THE embedded web view: CloudWeb.create(ctx, WebProfile.X), profiles, GPU probe, render-process recovery, shared BY REFERENCE.

modules._doc: Single source of truth for the Gradle module graph. settings.gradle iterates this list.

libs:headless-browser._doc: #1498 Headless Browser for agents, This App engine: HeadlessBrowserService, off-screen WebView sessions, signature-permission provider and loopback listener, shared BY REFERENCE.

libs:core._doc_dir: Shared BY REFERENCE from aa_cloud-superapp/libs/ — settings.gradle points projectDir here instead of at a local copy. Every app used to carry its own copy-pasted tree and they drifted: 6 apps sat 228 source lines behind superapp's updater. One directory, no sync step, no drift.

libs:devtools._doc_dir: Shared BY REFERENCE from aa_cloud-superapp/libs/, same as libs:core. Not listed in app.depends_on and not linked in app/build.gradle: libs:core pulls it in with an `api` dependency, which is what gives every app the constellation-wide debug API (127.0.0.1:38090+, own-process logcat) without per-app wiring that would drift.

libs:crash._doc: #1122 libs:core `api`s this module (the default crash handler, the local crash sink and the generic crash screen); listed so settings.gradle resolves the path and the ship workflow's path triggers see it, not linked in the app's own gradle.

libs:fleetconfig-model._doc: #873 libs:core `api`s this module (the setup provider every app serves, describe / export / apply / status); listed so settings.gradle resolves the path and the ship workflow's path triggers see it, not linked in the app's own gradle.

libs:browser._doc_dir: Shared BY REFERENCE from aa_cloud-superapp/libs/ - settings.gradle points projectDir here instead of at a local copy. browser was three byte-identical trees (superapp, browser, vault); nothing kept them in step, so a WebView fix had to be pasted three times or it silently reached one app.

libs:autofill._doc: The non-secret autofill SOT contract (a0_docs/eng-specs/autofill-3-tier.md). libs:browser reads Cloud Account's profiles and site rules through it (AUTOFILL_PROFILE_READ) and proposes a user-confirmed new address (AUTOFILL_PROFILE_WRITE).

libs:fleet-notify.comment: #1660 FleetNotify + KeepAliveStatus (the keep-alive and data-widget notifications), out of libs:core; linked by libs:updater (the Store batch foreground service), which this app compiles.

libs:updater._doc_dir: Shared BY REFERENCE from aa_cloud-superapp/libs/ — settings.gradle points projectDir here instead of at a local copy. Every app used to carry its own copy-pasted tree and they drifted: 6 apps sat 228 source lines behind superapp's updater. One directory, no sync step, no drift.

libs:ui-kit._doc_dir: #802 shared BY REFERENCE: the fleet's Compose kit. libs:browser draws its menu sheet, settings page and find bar with it.

libs:text-tools._doc_dir: #802 shared BY REFERENCE: the text-tools contract client (thin binder). libs:browser's Translate page row calls it; disabled with its reason when no app serves it.

libs:ai._doc_dir: #823 shared BY REFERENCE: the fleet's AI chat (renamed from libs:search-page). The Search add-on's Search & AI row draws its page over the browser, hosted by search/SearchPageScreen.kt (cloud-search's engines, the OpenRouter backend with the fleet Account's token, results opening as tabs) in the browser's kit palette; the assistant side panel and its consent card are its AiAssistantPanel, installed by search/AgentPanelScreen.kt.

libs:model-catalogue._doc_dir: libs:ai's `api` dependency (the shared agent descriptor its Agent picker lists). Listed so settings.gradle resolves the path; the browser declares no gateway agent and links nothing of it itself.

search-core._doc_dir: #802 I8 shared BY REFERENCE: cloud-search's plain-JVM core (its build.json::search reader and the OpenRouter chat protocol). The browser's search/chat routes use it; nothing is copied. Its own suite and PIT run in cloud-search's CI (this app's unit task is scoped to :app).

libs:ui-nav-bars._doc: #1164 shared navigation and theme design, shared BY REFERENCE.

libs:theme-background._doc: #1164 shared navigation and theme design, shared BY REFERENCE.

libs:bottomnav._doc_dir: #868 the fleet's bottom island + NavDecl, shared BY REFERENCE: MainActivity's island carries Browser | Search | Configs. The web tabs, the address bar and every overlay stay libs:browser's own UI.

libs:perms.comment: #1274 the permission contract: the catalogue asset (perms-catalogue.json: every runtime / special / app-op / adb-only grant with its SDK window, exact settings page, highlight key, adb line and the features that need it), the live status reader, the settings opener, the auto-request batch planner, the ADB block generator, PermsNeeds and the PermsLink deep link. Feature libs (wifi, bluetooth) use it to show a banner that opens the host's Permissions page; they never ask themselves. Renders nothing.

libs:bluetooth._doc: #1222 the Bluetooth stack behind the Web Bluetooth polyfill (navigator.bluetooth): libs:browser's WebBluetoothBridge drives its GattSession, shared BY REFERENCE with the SuperApp's Configs > Fleet > Bluetooth page (#1221).

libs:ui-icons._doc: #1160 the nav icon catalog (name to ImageVector, tinted or brand): every nav glyph of every app, shared BY REFERENCE; libs:bottomnav depends on it.

browser._doc: PER-APP browser content. libs:browser is shared BY REFERENCE (ac_cloud-vault/build.json names the same directory), so anything hardcoded in that module reaches every app that ever links it. The MECHANISM for pinning, grouping, history, suggestion and searching lives there; the CONTENT lives here. BrowserConfig.DEFAULT in the library pins NOTHING, so an app that supplies no block gets a browser with no pinned tabs rather than somebody else's homepage set. That boundary is the rule from #209: shared code is fine, one app's configuration turning up in another is not. Baked by app/build.gradle into BuildConfig.UI_BROWSER_CONFIG_B64 and handed to BrowserHostFragment.newInstance by MainActivity.
browser._doc_default_pinned_tabs: Pinned on FIRST RUN ONLY, in this order. BrowserTabPrefs.seedOnce sets a flag that is never cleared, so closing or unpinning one of these keeps it gone — a default that reappears every launch is an irritation, not a feature. The owner wrote the old fourth as 'localhost:800!'; the '!' is emphasis, not a digit, and :8000 is the port that actually answers on his phone.
browser._doc_local_pinned_tabs: The last four pins are the phone's own localhost servers, by their PRIVATE NAMES, in this order: Termux = termux.app (:8000, cloud-terminal-termux's $HOME via my-webserver), Nix = nix.app (:8001, cloud-terminal-nix's $HOME), Local = emulated.app (:8002, c3-webserver, phone storage /storage/emulated/0) and Cloud = cloud.app (:8003, c3-webserver's fleet diagnostics: the SuperApp's About, Logcat and Diagnose). THE name -> port map is ONE declaration, ac_cloud-c3-webserver/build.json::serving; app/build.gradle fails the build when a pin drifts from it or when its port disagrees with the owner's runtime port, and bakes the same map below as private_names. A name is resolved by this browser through the c3-webserver's own DNS server on loopback (udp 127.0.0.1:5354, libs:browser PrivateNames), only for these four exact names and only inside this app; it is never handed to the system resolver (termux.app is a real website). These are first-run pins: a phone that already seeded its tabs keeps the localhost pins it has. Each default_pinned_tabs entry is {url, title} with title = its name here, so the tab shows that name instead of the page title (libs:browser also still accepts a plain URL string); app/build.gradle checks the title too.
browser._doc_private_names: Baked at build time by app/build.gradle from ac_cloud-c3-webserver/build.json::serving as ui.browser.private_names = {dns:{host,port}, names:{<name>: <port>}}; absent from this file on purpose, so the map has exactly one declaration. libs:browser PrivateNames reads it.
browser._doc_search_engines: Address-bar engines. {q} is where the URL-encoded query goes, so an engine whose query parameter is not last still works. default_engine is the SHIPPED default; BrowserSettings persists the user's own pick and BrowserConfig.engine() resolves an unknown or unset id back to this one. suggest (optional) is the engine's query-suggestion feed (https, {q}, OpenSearch JSON), asked only while the search_suggestions setting is on (BrowserRemoteSuggest); an engine without one simply offers its search row.
browser._doc_settings: #802 THE SETTINGS CATALOGUE: every user setting, declared once. libs:browser BrowserSettingsCatalogue parses it (baked inside UI_BROWSER_CONFIG_B64 with the rest of this block), BrowserSettings stores the user's choice in the `browser_settings` prefs (declared in the fleet manifest, so FleetConfig moves every key to a new phone), /api/browser/settings* serve and set it, and ./build.sh catalogue renders docs/settings-catalogue.md from it. type: bool|int|string|enum|set; class: config (migrates) | device (stays). values_from: search_engines takes the enum and its default from search_engines/default_engine above. A key is only declared once something reads it (test-browser-settings-catalogue.sh holds that).

settings.label: Search engine
settings.doc: Where a typed query that is not a URL goes.

settings.label: Homepage
settings.doc: What an empty New tab opens. Empty = nothing (the dialog just closes).

settings.label: Reopen last tab on launch
settings.doc: Launch into the last active tab instead of the tab grid.

settings.label: Desktop site
settings.doc: Desktop user agent + wide viewport for every page.

settings.label: Text size (%)
settings.doc: WebSettings.textZoom, in percent.

settings.label: JavaScript
settings.doc: Run page scripts. Off breaks most sites; per-site shields come later.

settings.label: Load images
settings.doc: Off saves data on metered networks.

settings.label: Block third-party cookies
settings.doc: CookieManager.setAcceptThirdPartyCookies(false) on every page.

settings.label: Download folder
settings.doc: Sub-folder of the phone's Downloads that downloads land in. Empty = Downloads itself. Device-class: a path on this phone.

settings.label: New tabs are private
settings.doc: A new tab opens private: no history, no preview, no HTTP cache. Cookies are shared with normal tabs (Android WebView keeps them per process).

settings.label: Autofill
settings.doc: Pages expose their fields to Android's Autofill Framework (Cloud Vault fills logins and cards there), and Fill from profile is offered.

settings.label: Fill contact & address forms
settings.doc: Tier 2 DOM autofill (a0_docs/eng-specs/autofill-3-tier.md): focusing a name, email, phone or address field offers a chip that fills the form from your Cloud Account profiles. Never passwords, codes or cards (Cloud Vault fills those), never a login form's email. Private tabs show a chip that names no profile and fill only on an explicit pick.

settings.label: Offer to save new addresses
settings.doc: After you submit an address form with an address Cloud Account does not have yet, ask whether to save it there. Nothing is saved without your tap, and never from a private tab.

settings.label: Summarize with
settings.doc: #823 Where Summarize the page runs: model = the fleet's AI model (needs the network and the fleet Account's OpenRouter token; falls back on device when it cannot answer); on_device = on the phone, offline (ML Kit's summarizer where the phone has it, else the page's key sentences).

settings.label: Enabled add-ons
settings.doc: The add-ons that are on (Settings ▸ Add-ons). Default: each add-on's default_enabled.

settings.label: Search suggestions
settings.doc: While you type in the address bar, ask the default search engine for query suggestions (what you type is sent to it). Off = only the search row and your own history.

settings.label: Tab strip
settings.doc: A row of small tab icons under the address bar: the tabs of the current group, and a + that opens a new tab in the same group.

settings.label: Translate with
settings.doc: Which engine Translate page uses, in place on the page. On-device ML = the fleet's translation library in Cloud Writer / Cloud Keyboard (offline, private). OpenRouter = the model chosen in that app's AI routing (needs the network; the key stays in that app). Summarise by topics needs OpenRouter.

settings.label: Translate into
settings.doc: The language Translate page and Summarise by topics write in.

settings.label: Offline site depth
settings.doc: Save site offline follows same-site links this many levels from the page you are on (0 = only that page).

settings.label: Offline site: max pages
settings.doc: Save site offline stops after this many pages.

settings.label: Offline site: max size (MB)
settings.doc: Save site offline stops when the copy reaches this size.

settings.label: Downloads at a time
settings.doc: How many downloads (and torrents) transfer at once; the rest wait in the queue.

settings.label: Download on Wi-Fi only
settings.doc: Downloads wait (and resume by themselves) until the phone is on Wi-Fi or Ethernet.

settings.label: Download on metered networks
settings.doc: Off = downloads wait for an unmetered network (no mobile data, no metered hotspot).

settings.label: Download speed limit (KB/s)
settings.doc: Shared by every HTTP download; torrents get the same cap for their downloads. 0 = no limit.

settings.label: Connections per large file
settings.doc: A large file on a server that accepts byte ranges downloads over this many connections at once; 1 = always one connection.

settings.label: Save to cloud-shared-store
settings.doc: When cloud-shared-store is installed, finished downloads go there instead of the phone's Download folder. Without it, this does nothing.

settings.label: Seed torrents after downloading
settings.doc: A finished torrent keeps uploading to other peers until a limit below is reached (or you turn seeding off on its row); its files are published to Download/ when seeding stops.

settings.label: Seed until ratio (%)
settings.doc: Stop seeding once this share of the torrent's size has been uploaded (100 = 1.0); 0 = no ratio limit.

settings.label: Seed for at most (minutes)
settings.doc: Stop seeding after this long; 0 = no time limit.

settings.label: Torrent upload limit (KB/s)
settings.doc: Upload speed cap for every torrent together; 0 = no limit. Downloads use the download speed limit above.

settings.label: Block trackers
settings.doc: Subresource requests to the declared tracker hosts are answered empty on every site. A site can allow them (page menu > This site > Block trackers here).

settings.label: Remember values typed on a site
settings.doc: After you submit a form, offer to remember a value you typed that is not generic personal data (a customer number, a member ID) for that site and form only. Never from a private tab, never a password, card, code or search box.

settings.label: Offer to add new details to a profile
settings.doc: After you submit a form with a name, address, phone, email, birth date or document that none of your profiles holds, ask which profile to add it to. Nothing is saved without your tap, and never from a private tab.

settings.label: Offer to save passwords
settings.doc: After a sign-in or sign-up form is submitted with a new or changed password, ask whether to save it on this phone (encrypted).

settings.label: Ask for fingerprint or screen lock
settings.doc: Before a saved password or card is revealed or filled, ask for the fingerprint, face or screen lock. Off means anyone holding the unlocked phone can fill them.

settings.label: Offer to save cards
settings.doc: After a checkout form with a card is submitted, ask whether to save the card on this phone (encrypted).

settings.label: Use Cloud Vault for passwords & cards
settings.doc: The browser fills from its own store first, then asks Cloud Vault (through Android's autofill); what Cloud Vault fills wins over the local copy, and a new password or card is also handed to Cloud Vault's save. Off = local only. Cloud Vault not installed or locked = local only, with the reason shown.

settings.label: Backend
settings.doc: Where agent browser calls run (#1498): Cloudflare-Browser-Run (the #1474 backend and store keys), Cloudy-Browser-Headless (the container on oci-apps) or This App (off-screen WebView on this phone, the default).

settings.label: Cloudy-Browser-Headless URL (store key name)
settings.doc: The NAME of the encrypted-store key that holds the container URL (https, mesh path route). The value is never kept here.

settings.label: Cloudy-Browser-Headless bearer (store key name)
settings.doc: The NAME of the encrypted-store key that holds the container bearer token. The value is never kept here; the vault holds it by name.

settings.label: Max sessions (This App)
settings.doc: Open sessions at once on this phone, 1 to 8. A new session over the limit is refused.

settings.label: Idle stop (seconds)
settings.doc: The service stops, and a session closes, after this long without a command (15 to 1800).

settings.label: Per-call timeout (seconds)
settings.doc: A command that takes longer answers a timeout (1 to 120).

settings.label: DevTools / CDP (debug, opt-in)
settings.doc: Lets Playwright or Puppeteer connectOverCDP to the phone engine: WebView debugging on, the DevTools socket relayed to a loopback port, bearer-gated, off by itself after the minutes below. Default off.

settings.label: DevTools / CDP auto-off (minutes)
settings.doc: CDP switches itself off after this long (1 to 60).

browser._doc_favourites: #893 THE FAVOURITES SEED (Fav = the bookmarks, one store). Not typed here: app/build.gradle EXPANDS `sources` at build time into `items` (title, url, group) from the fleet's own declaration, aa_cloud-superapp/data/services_public.json (every public edge endpoint) and services_private.json (the mesh-internal HTTP endpoints, shown and opened as declared, they answer on the mesh), and bakes the result inside UI_BROWSER_CONFIG_B64, so a seed change rebuilds only Cloud Browser. BrowserBookmarks.applySeed adds each entry ONCE (first run, and any entry a later `version` brings), never overwrites an edit and never re-adds what the user deleted. No credentials: only the url as declared. #1458 The "GH Pages" chip is NOT baked: it is read at runtime from `feed` (pages.json in the public hub repo diegonmarcos/front-html, generated there from the GitHub API), cached as the last good copy, and merged once per entry like the rest. test/test-browser-pages-hub.sh holds the wiring.
browser._doc_favourites_v3: #1422 VERSION 3: the seed is ONE derived file, app/src/main/assets/favourites_catalog.json (`catalog`, an asset: too big for BuildConfig), written by tools/gen-favourites-catalog.py from the registries (`filters[].from`: GitHub Pages list, SuperApp services_public / services_private filed under the SuperApp Cloud dashboard categories, the cloud-webserver serving endpoint, the SuperApp phone_sections / phone_folders taxonomy the Store's Phone > Apps reads). Each filter is a chip under the Favourites title; an item's group is '<chip label>/<sub-folder>'. A `legacy_groups` bookmark the seed also carries moves to its new group once. test/test-browser-favourites-catalog.sh fails when the committed file is stale.
browser._doc_user_agents: #802 the user-agent strings desktop_mode switches between, declared here rather than in libs:browser (they used to be literals in BrowserHostFragment). #1421 NO `mobile` agent: the pinned 'Pixel 8 / Chrome 124' string disagreed with the real WebView's version and with its own Sec-CH-UA client hints, so UA-sniffing scripts served the wrong bundle (or none) and bot checks challenged; mobile mode uses WebView's own default agent (WebSettings.getDefaultUserAgent). Desktop mode is the user's explicit request for a desktop page.

user_agents.desktop: Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Linux x86_64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/124.0.0.0 Safari/537.36 CloudSuperApp/1.0

browser._doc_palette: #802 the seven KitPalette roles the Compose surfaces (menu sheet, settings, find bar, panels) paint with; the browser's purple-on-black chrome.
browser._doc_reader_css: #802 the stylesheet reader mode renders the extracted article with (assets/browser/reader.js does the extraction).
browser._doc_menu: #802/#900/#1401 BROWSING TOOLS, declared: the page-tools dropdown (section ids match the tab labels: actions, page_tools, site_data, site_perms, dev_tools): the sheet opened by the icon at the far right of the tab row (the app bar's ⋮ opens Configs). It holds ONLY what acts on the current page or domain, as five TABS in this order: Actions (navigation, reload/refresh, bookmark, copy URL, open in another app, home screen, pin/download site), Page Tools (grouped by `category`: Reading, Save & Export, Find & Share, View mode, Autofill; add-on page rows join here), Site Data (cookies and storage of this site, clear, autocomplete, trackers, images), Site Perms (one row, Perms: every permission a site can request), Dev Tools (console, network, elements, storage, graphics stats, remote debugging, JavaScript for this site). Global things live on the Configs pages.

requires_why.can_go_back: no earlier page in this tab
requires_why.can_go_forward: no later page in this tab
requires_why.text_tools: no app on this phone serves the fleet's text tools
requires_why.can_be_default: already the default browser, or Android offers no browser role
requires_why.profile_present: the profile is empty: Settings ▸ Profile imports one, or apply the Account

items.label: Hard refresh (cache, cookies, storage)
items._doc: #1141 first visit again: clears this site's HTTP cache, cookies, DOM and local storage and Service Workers, then reloads past the cache.

items.label: Light refresh (cache)
items._doc: #1141 clears the HTTP cache and this site's Service Workers, keeps cookies and storage, reloads past the cache.

items.label: Site data: cookies & storage…
items._doc: This site's cookies and its storage (local/session storage, IndexedDB, service workers, cache storage), each its own box. Never autofill data: that is Configs > Autocomplete. a0_docs/eng-specs/autofill-3-tier.md 3.1.

items.label: Graphics: FPS, draw calls, GPU (debugger)
items._doc: Opens Dev Tools on its Graphics tab: injected JS samples FPS, frame time, WebGL draw calls, triangles and the GPU name of the current page; n/a with a note when the page blocks injection or has no WebGL.

browser._doc_configs: #900 CONFIGS, declared. Each Configs page (ui.sections[configs].pages = the top tabs = settings_sections) draws the settings whose `section` is that page, then its `rows` (global actions that used to sit in the page menu; same runAction branches), then its `native` blocks (the Autocomplete, Passwords, Cards, Vault and About sections libs:browser draws itself). An add-on menu entry with scope:global and page:<id> joins that page's rows. The page dropdown holds none of these (test-browser-page-menu.sh).
browser._doc_site_permissions: #802/#1401 EVERY permission a site can request, one per-site state (ask/allow/deny) each, plus a global default (stored as host `*`). The most-used come first (`top`), then all the rest. `webview: true` rows are enforced (`enforced_by` names the WebView hook); `webview: false` rows are declared but not supported in WebView, `why` says so on the Perms page.

site_permissions.label: Notifications
site_permissions.why: not supported in WebView: Android WebView has no Notification API, so a page can never ask for it.

site_permissions.label: Pop-ups and redirects
site_permissions.enforced_by: WebChromeClient.onCreateWindow (ask = only on a user gesture)

site_permissions.label: Clipboard read/write
site_permissions.why: not supported in WebView: WebView gives the app no permission hook for the async Clipboard API; it decides on its own.

site_permissions.label: Downloads / automatic downloads
site_permissions.enforced_by: WebView DownloadListener (ask = a prompt per download)

site_permissions.label: Motion & orientation sensors
site_permissions.why: not supported in WebView: WebView delivers devicemotion/deviceorientation with no permission hook.

site_permissions.label: MIDI / MIDI SysEx
site_permissions.enforced_by: WebChromeClient.onPermissionRequest (MIDI_SYSEX; plain MIDI is not gated by WebView)

site_permissions.label: Bluetooth
site_permissions.why: not supported in WebView: WebView has no Web Bluetooth; the browser's own shim asks with its chooser on every use.

site_permissions.label: USB
site_permissions.why: not supported in WebView: WebView has no WebUSB; the browser's own hardware shim asks with its chooser on every use.

site_permissions.label: Serial
site_permissions.why: not supported in WebView: WebView has no Web Serial; the browser's own hardware shim asks with its chooser on every use.

site_permissions.label: HID
site_permissions.why: not supported in WebView: WebView has no WebHID; the browser's own hardware shim asks with its chooser on every use.

site_permissions.label: NFC
site_permissions.why: not supported in WebView: WebView has no Web NFC.

site_permissions.label: Background sync
site_permissions.why: not supported in WebView: WebView does not implement Background Sync.

site_permissions.label: Idle detection
site_permissions.why: not supported in WebView: WebView does not implement the Idle Detection API.

site_permissions.label: Screen wake lock
site_permissions.why: not supported in WebView: WebView gives the app no permission hook for the Screen Wake Lock API.

site_permissions.label: Window management
site_permissions.why: not supported in WebView: WebView has one window per view; the Window Management API is absent.

site_permissions.label: Local fonts
site_permissions.why: not supported in WebView: WebView does not implement the Local Font Access API.

site_permissions.label: File system access
site_permissions.why: not supported in WebView: WebView has no File System Access API; a file input always opens the system picker.

site_permissions.label: Payment handler
site_permissions.why: not supported in WebView: WebView does not implement Payment Handler.

site_permissions.label: Device use (VR/AR)
site_permissions.why: not supported in WebView: WebView does not implement WebXR.

site_permissions.label: Display capture (screen share)
site_permissions.why: not supported in WebView: WebView does not implement getDisplayMedia.

site_permissions.label: Picture-in-picture
site_permissions.why: not supported in WebView: WebView does not implement the Picture-in-Picture API.

site_permissions.label: Ads
site_permissions.why: not supported in WebView: WebView has no ad filter; Trackers blocks the declared tracker hosts.

site_permissions.label: Intrusive ads
site_permissions.why: not supported in WebView: WebView has no Better Ads filter.

site_permissions.label: Sound
site_permissions.why: not supported in WebView: WebView has no per-page mute.

site_permissions.label: Insecure content
site_permissions.enforced_by: WebSettings.mixedContentMode (allow = always, ask = compatibility, block = never)

site_permissions.label: Federated identity / third-party sign-in
site_permissions.why: not supported in WebView: WebView does not implement FedCM; sign-in pop-ups follow Pop-ups and redirects.

site_permissions.label: Storage access
site_permissions.why: not supported in WebView: WebView does not implement the Storage Access API.

browser._doc_tab_thumbnails: Tab-switcher snapshots, declared once. scale = capture size relative to the WebView (0.25 = a quarter of each side, RGB_565). memory_kb = memory LRU bound; disk_kb = disk cache bound under cacheDir/tabs (oldest file evicted first); quality = lossy WebP quality of the disk copy. incognito: 'skip' = a private tab is never captured; 'memory' = captured, kept in the memory LRU only, never written to disk. Captured when a page finishes loading, when a tab is left, and when the switcher opens; deleted when the tab closes. Read by libs:browser TabThumbConfig.
browser._doc_tracker_hosts: #900 Block trackers here: a subresource request to one of these hosts (or a subdomain) is answered empty while the site's `trackers` permission is deny (the default; setting block_trackers moves the default). Content of THIS app: libs:browser ships no list (BrowserTrackers matches whatever it is handed).
browser._doc_clear_data: #802 the boxes of Clear browsing data; each id is one branch of libs:browser BrowserClearData.clear (test-browser-privacy-wired.sh holds that).
browser._doc_addons: #802 THE ADD-ONS, declared. libs:browser BrowserAddons parses them: permissions are words from BrowserAddons.PERMISSIONS (shown on the Add-ons page), requires_package is a fleet app the add-on needs installed, menu rows join the menu's `addons` section and require the fact addon:<id> (enabled + its app installed), so a disabled add-on's rows say why. Each add-on's own block (remote, limits, tools) is handed to it verbatim. test-browser-addons-declared.sh holds every row to its runAction branch and every permission to the vocabulary.

addons.label: Web scraper
addons.doc: Extract a table from the page by CSS selector, follow next-page links, export CSV; or ask the server (scrappers-api) to crawl.
addons._doc_remote: scrappers-api's generic crawl over the WireGuard mesh (cloud-u-containers user-data_scrappers-api main.py: POST /scrape/crawl {url, selector}, synchronous, answers {ok, written, summary.matched}; rows stay on the server). The mesh address is the service's declared container port (cloud-infra build-scrappers-api.json: scrappers-api.mesh.diegonmarcos.com :3020 on oci-apps 10.0.0.6); the public route is behind two-factor Authelia, so the phone uses the mesh.

addons.label: Search
addons.doc: Cloud Search's engines open their results in a new tab; its AI chat answers over the fleet API with the fleet Account's OpenRouter token (read per call, never stored).
addons._doc_config_from: app/build.gradle copies ../ac_cloud-search/build.json::search.engines into this add-on's `engines` and bakes the whole search block as BuildConfig.SEARCH_CONFIG_B64: ONE declaration, cloud-search's. No engine URL or model is spelled here or in Kotlin.

addons.label: AI
addons.doc: An assistant that reads and acts on the open page with the declared tools. Reading tools run freely; every tool that clicks, types, navigates or changes tabs or bookmarks asks first, naming the action and the site. It never fills passwords or card data and never sees the vault or the autofill profile.
addons._doc_model: The model is cloud-search's search.ai.default_model unless `model` is set here; the token is the fleet Account's OpenRouter key, read per turn (the Search add-on's path).
addons._doc_summarize: #823 Summarize the page (menu row, the summarize_page tool, /api/browser/ai/summarize) on the user's route, setting summarize_route: model = the fleet model (this add-on's model) with the fleet Account token read per call; on_device = ML Kit's on-device summarizer where the phone has it (AICore / Gemini Nano), else an extractive summary of the page's own sentences. The #799/#800 rule: a model route that cannot run (offline) or fails falls back on device when fallback is true, and every answer names route, engine, fell_back and reason.

summarize.prompt: Summarize this web page in %d short bullet points. Answer in the page's language.

addons._doc_tools: Each tool: mutating:true must be confirm:true (test-browser-agent-consent.sh). route model = the result goes back to the model. Names are the wire names the model sees.

addons.label: Vault autofill
addons.doc: Logins and cards are filled by Cloud Vault (the fleet's Bitwarden) through Android's autofill: this browser never holds a password. The add-on shows whether Cloud Vault is the autofill service, asks it to fill the focused login, and opens it.
addons._doc_requires_fleet: app/build.gradle resolves the fleet id to its package (aa_cloud-superapp/data/constellation-fleet.json) into requires_package and the manifest's <queries>; no package is spelled here or in Kotlin.

browser._doc_settings_sections: #886/#900 Configs is organised BY PAGE: each setting's `section` is one of these ids = one of the top tabs of the Configs section (ui.sections[configs].pages, same ids, same order: test-browser-page-menu.sh holds that). A page with nothing in it is still a tab (its rows or native blocks fill it).

ui._doc_nav: #868/#1493 THE nav declaration (libs:bottomnav NavDecl): ui.bottom_nav is the island, ui.sections[] what each item opens, ui.default_section where the app opens. Island order (#1493): Weby, Cloudy, Browser, Tabs, Domains. browser = BrowserHostFragment's page (its address bar, tab strip and overlays are the lib's own UI, so the section has no pages), tabs = the tab switcher (BrowserHostFragment.openTabs, #886), weby = the bookmarks as a launcher icon grid in folders, seeded from the SuperApp phone apps, cloudy = Cloudy-Public GH-Pages | Cloudy-Private Webserver, domains = Headless Browsers | Files Cached | Perms&Actions | History | Visited; those three are drawn by MainActivity over the host from sites/ (top tabs = ui.sections[<id>].pages). favourites and search stay declared sections reached from the first row (the AI icon opens Search), no longer island items; configs = the browser settings over the host (showSettings), one top tab per Configs page: ui.sections[configs].pages = settings_sections (#900). MainActivity feeds the island from NavDecl and follows the host's overlays so the pill goes back to Browser when one closes.

sections.label: Weby
sections._doc: #1493 the bookmarks as a launcher icon grid in folders (sites/WebyPage.kt). Seeded from the Cloud SuperApp Phone WebApps declaration (aa_cloud-superapp/data/phone-webapps.json, #1466), read at BUILD time by app/build.gradle into SITES_DECL_B64: same groups, same order, never copied by hand.

sections.label: Cloudy
sections._doc: #1493/#1531 the owner's sites, four tabs: GH Pages (declared repos + front-html pages.json), Local Webserver (the pages the phone's Cloud-Webserver serves, and a link that opens its APK), Cloudy Private URLs and Cloudy Public URLs (the fleet's Caddy routes, ac_cloud-c3 data/routes.json: the mesh address / the public address of each). All derived at build time (ui.cloudy).

sections.label: Domains
sections._doc: #1493 what the browser knows per site (sites/DomainsPage.kt): cached files, permissions and clear actions, history per day, visited domains. Texts and actions are ui.domains.

pages.label: General
pages._doc: #1443 the fleet Configs tabs: General | Perms | About (libs:ui-nav-bars FleetConfigsPageBody, drawn by MainActivity over the host), then the browser's own pages.

weby._doc: #1493 Weby's words. Its folders and tiles are NOT here: app/build.gradle derives them from aa_cloud-superapp (ui.sections[phone].phone_app_groups + data/phone-webapps.json); the user's edits are the weby_bookmarks prefs.

texts.remove_folder: Remove this folder and everything in it?

weby._doc_icons: #1531 each tile's icon is its website's own picture (manifest icons, then apple-touch-icon, then favicon; sites/WebyIcons.kt), fetched on demand and kept in the app's files (weby_icons/); a tile with no website or no picture is grey with its initial. website_meta_keys is NOT here: app/build.gradle bakes the SuperApp's ui.app_urls.website_meta_keys (the declared website lookup for an app whose phone-webapps entry has no address). icon_overrides: tile id (package) or host -> icon URL, used instead of the lookup.

cloudy._doc: #1493 Cloudy. pages_url = front-html's Pages list (the owner's GitHub Pages, public ones, refreshed over the network and kept in the cloudy_cache prefs); the declared repos' Pages (ac_cloud-c3 data/repos_declared.json) and the Cloud-Webserver's serving map, Pages sub-pages and Repos store (ac_cloud-c3-webserver/build.json) are read by app/build.gradle. webserver_base_role = the serving endpoint the Webserver's own pages are served on.
cloudy._doc_webserver: The Cloud-Webserver's package and launcher activity are NOT here: app/build.gradle reads the package from ac_cloud-c3-webserver build.json serving.keepalive and the launcher activity from its AndroidManifest.xml.

texts.ws_not_installed: Cloud-Webserver is not installed on this phone. Install it from the constellation store first.

domains._doc: #1493 Domains: the per-site actions (ids are the SiteActions plans: cookies, media, cache, storage, reset_perms), what counts as media (cached content types), the History and Visited switches and the words.

ui._doc_debug_api: #802 Routes on the fleet debug API (libs:devtools AppDebugServer, loopback + fleet token): /api/browser/settings, settings/catalogue, settings/set?key=&value=, tabs, tabs/open|close|pin?url=, history?n=, history/clear?confirm=1, menu, menu/act?id=&q=&value=, page/find?q=, page/text?n=, page/reader, bookmarks, bookmarks/add?url=&title=&folder=, bookmarks/remove?url=, bookmarks/folders, bookmarks/folder/rename?from=&to=, bookmarks/folder/delete?folder=, downloads, downloads/enqueue?url=, downloads/clear, sites?host=, sites/set?host=&perm=&value=, privacy/clear?history=1&cookies=1&cache=1&storage=1&previews=1&downloads=1&url=&confirm=1, profile (masked), profile/import (POST body, format=csv|firefox|bitwarden|vault|native), profile/clear?confirm=1, profile/fill (dry: the fields the live page offers and which profile key each would get, never a value), addons, addons/set?id=&on=, scraper/run?css=&attr=&pages=&next=, scraper/last, scraper/remote?url=&css=. The full list is served by /api/docs. No op is named `state` (update-ack-guard owns GET /api/state).

web._doc: #876 Cloud Browser as a Kotlin/Wasm page (web/ is its own gradle root; the shared libs' pure-Compose sources arrive through the ab_cloud-libs-shared/web composite). Rendered into 1_cicd/src/cicd/ship-cloud-browser-wasm.yml by the workflow generator: `./gradlew wasmJsBrowserDistribution` in `dir`, tested by test/test-browser-web.sh, `build/dist/wasmJs/productionExecutable` zipped to `artifact` and attached to the rolling release as `gh_asset`. A mocked page: the island and tab strips are ui.bottom_nav / ui.sections as the Android shell reads them, the first section shows mock data and the rest say they live in the Android app. The APK's own ship ignores this directory.

tests._doc: What CI runs to prove this app works. Read by 1_cicd/src/scripts/cloud-android-test-engine.sh. Before this block existed the browser had NO tests at all and its ship workflow asserted only that Gradle exited 0.

shell._doc_requires: Tools the testers shell out to, checked BEFORE any of them runs. A missing tool does not make a tester fail - it makes the tester answer from the tool's absence. These testers use python3 for whole-string and JSON comparisons; naming it converts a silent green into a loud red.

unit._doc: The JVM unit test task. NO EMULATOR: src/test/ is the JVM source set; only src/androidTest/ needs a device. SCOPED to :app: on purpose - an unscoped testDebugUnitTest also runs libs:devtools' suite, and this app's release must not go red over a sibling library's assertions. debug and not release so the task reuses the variant a push to main actually builds, and never configures the release signingConfig, which needs the vault keystore.

auto_update._doc_max_installs_per_pass: Most install sessions ONE unattended background pass may open. A background pass cannot show the system install dialog (Android 10+ blocks background activity starts), so each install it starts leaves a tap-to-install notification holding a PackageInstaller session until the user answers it. Unbounded, one pass over the 40-entry fleet opens 40 and the installer hits Android's 50-session cap - 'Too many active sessions for UID'. The remainder is picked up by the next pass. User-initiated 'Update all' is NOT capped: it runs in the foreground where the dialog appears and sessions resolve at once.

analytics._doc: Consumed by :libs:analytics, which reads THIS file (rootDir) at build time and bakes the values into BuildConfig. Both backends are single-site today, so every app reports into the same site and is told apart by .app — give each app its own site_id once per-app sites exist in Umami/Matomo.

_doc_fleet_agents: This app's agents, in the fleet agent registry's one shape (aa_cloud-superapp/build.json::_doc_fleet_agents). Consolidated into aa_cloud-superapp/data/fleet-agents.json by 1_cicd/src/scripts/cloud-android-fleet-agents.py and shown in Cloud SuperApp ▸ Configs ▸ Apps ▸ Agents ▸ Fleet agents.

fleet_agents.trigger: on demand (AI chat on the open page)
fleet_agents.summary: Reads and acts on the open page with the declared tools; every tool that changes something asks first.

status.reason: the agent runs inside the open tab; Cloud Browser exposes no status for it

fleet_agents.name: Browser agent door
fleet_agents.summary: agentapi: opens a URL for the person, or reads a page text read-only (#913).

configs_pages._doc: Configs > General and Configs > About (libs:ui-nav-bars fleetconfigs, rule 1_cicd/src/data/configs-pages.json, #1352 v2). general.sections: the anchors of the one General page, in order (perms, battery, storage, notifications, ui, language are required; app opens this app's own Configs; update is added after perms by default). about: the hand-written part of the extensive About: tagline, description, features, screens, guide, privacy, backends (ids of ac_cloud-account/build.json::fleet_endpoints, resolved to mesh URLs at build time), related fleet apps, credits for a fork. Permissions, data stores, crash/analytics libs, name, icon, version, build sha and date, repo, licence, origin, crash sink, debug API and changelog are derived, never typed here.

sections.label: App
sections.note: This app's own settings: General, Search, Privacy & Security, Site settings, Autocomplete, Passwords, Payment, Downloads, Appearance, Tabs, Sync & Vault, Advanced, About.

about.tagline: A focused browser with the vault's passwords
about.description: Cloud Browser is a standalone WebView browser lifted out of the SuperApp into its own app. Tabs survive restarts, the address bar searches with the engine you choose, favourites are one tap away, and passwords and autofill come from the owner's self-hosted vault instead of a third-party sync service. It exists to browse the fleet's own web pages and the open web with the same identity and without an ad-tech browser in the middle.
features: Passwords and autofill from the vault

screens.name: Browser
screens.what: The page itself with the address bar.

screens.name: Scrapers
screens.what: Site Files (every file a site left: cache, downloads, saved pages), Apify (actors, Store search, runs, datasets) and SelfHosted (Music, YouTube Download, scrappers-api).

screens.name: Configs
screens.what: Site settings, privacy, downloads and appearance (the top bar's ⋮).

guide: Type an address or a search in the bar at the top.
Long-press a page to add it to Fav.
Sign in to the vault in Configs to fill passwords.
Open Tabs to switch or close tabs.
about.privacy: No ads and no third-party trackers. A crash report is saved on the phone and sent only to the phone's own C3 WebServer over loopback; nothing leaves the device unless you share it. Usage analytics are opt-in and off by default; when allowed, events go only to the owner's self-hosted Umami and Matomo. It talks only to the fleet services listed below, over the private mesh first.

related.why: Signs in to the fleet and holds the tokens and secrets this app reads.

perms._doc: #1360 every grant this app needs, by libs:perms catalogue id (needs), and the fleet apps that do work for it with the grants THEY must hold (helpers). The ONE declaration: generated into assets/app-perms.json (cloud-android-perms-guard.py --write), drawn by Configs > General > Perms (libs:perms AppPermsSection) with live state, Grant / Open and Grant all, asked at first run (first_run), and reported as 'Missing permission X - Grant' when an operation fails (PermsGate). perms-guard fails when code uses a gated API or another app's engine that is not declared here, or when the manifest and this list disagree.
